notes: BATCH_008 Banking and Financial Awareness, topic package 1 (Banking Fundamentals, History of Banking in India, Reserve Bank of India, RBI Functions, Monetary Policy, Repo Rate, Reverse Repo Rate, CRR, SLR, Bank Rate, Inflation): 64 original questions, IDs BANK_BFA_001404 to BANK_BFA_001467. Built from RBI pages opened on 2026-11-06 (consolidated Commercial Banks Directions of 28 Nov 2025 on deposits, advances and voluntary amalgamation, the Miscellaneous Directions' DEA Fund chapter, the liquidity management framework of 30 Sep 2025, MPC resolutions Feb 2025-Oct 2026, RBI press releases and auction results, FAQs on currency, cheque clearing and Government banking, RBI's history chronology, Governors' profiles and Bank Rate/CRR/SLR table) and MoSPI/DPIIT price releases. Only current rules are tested; older rules appear only as explicit history. Computed answers are re-derived with asserts in tools/packages/BFA_pkg1.py. ai:independent-check marks only questions a separate fresh solver answered blind and matched with confidence.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's profile of its Governors, during whose tenure as Governor were six private sector banks nationalised (April 1980) and priority sector lending targets introduced?

solution.explanation: Dr. I. G. Patel was Governor from 1 December 1977 to 15 September 1982. RBI's profile records that his tenure saw the nationalisation of six private sector banks (15 April 1980), the introduction of priority sector lending targets and the merger of the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporations.
steps: Governor then: Dr. I. G. Patel
solution.why_others_wrong: M. Narasimham served only May–November 1977; Dr. Manmohan Singh took over in September 1982; K. R. Puri served 1975–77, when RRBs were set up.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Dr. I. G. Patel

fact_checks.claim: Dr. I G Patel, 01-12-1977 to 15-09-1982: During his tenure six private sector banks were nationalised, targets for priority sector lending introduced
15 Apr 1980: Six private sector banks nationalised

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The 'Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector', set up in 1994, was chaired by:

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology for 1991–2000 lists the 1994 'Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector' under R. N. Malhotra, a former RBI Governor (1985–1990). Its report paved the way for opening insurance to the private sector.
steps: 1994, insurance sector reform → R. N. Malhotra Committee
solution.why_others_wrong: Narasimham chaired the financial-system committees of 1991 and 1998; Chakravarty reviewed the monetary system (1985); Rangarajan was RBI Governor in 1994.
solution.final_answer: Option A: R. N. Malhotra

fact_checks.claim: 1994: 'Committee on Reform of the Insurance Sector', RN Malhotra

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's Commercial Banks – Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025, which govern the merger of one banking company with another, are issued under which section of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 (along with Section 35A)?

solution.concept: Statutory basis of voluntary bank mergers
solution.explanation: Voluntary amalgamation of banking companies is governed by Section 44A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949. RBI's 2025 Directions are issued under Sections 44A and 35A, and the scheme approved by shareholders is submitted to RBI for sanction.
steps: Voluntary amalgamation of banking companies → BR Act Section 44A
solution.why_others_wrong: Section 45 deals with RBI-framed (compulsory) schemes of reconstruction or amalgamation; Section 22 is licensing; Section 26A is the DEA Fund.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Section 44A

fact_checks.claim: In exercise of the powers conferred by Section 44A and Section 35A of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949 ... RBI ... hereby issues the Directions (Commercial Banks - Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under Section 44A(3) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, as set out in RBI's Voluntary Amalgamation Directions, 2025, what is a shareholder who voted against a bank merger entitled to once RBI sanctions the scheme?

options.text: To block the merger if he holds more than 10% of the shares
To claim, within three months of the sanction, the value of his shares as determined by RBI, which is final
To claim, within one year, the market price of his shares on the date of sanction
To approach the NCLT within 30 days to have the share value fixed afresh

solution.explanation: A dissenting shareholder may, within three months from the date of RBI's sanction, claim from the bank concerned the value of his shares as determined by RBI while sanctioning the scheme. RBI's determination is final for all purposes.
solution.why_others_wrong: A single dissenter cannot block a scheme passed by the required majority; the period is three months, not a year; the value is fixed by RBI, not re-fixed by the NCLT.
solution.final_answer: Option B: To claim, within three months of the sanction, the value of his shares as determined by RBI, which is final

fact_checks.claim: In terms of Section 44A (3) of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, a dissenting shareholder is entitled, in the event of the scheme being sanctioned by RBI, to claim within three months from the date of sanction ... the value of the shares ... as determined by RBI when sanctioning the scheme. Such determination by the RBI of the value of the shares shall be final for all purposes

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's history of its Governors and its chronology:
I. The nationalisation of 14 major commercial banks in 1969 did not have the endorsement of the Reserve Bank.
II. An Agricultural Credit Board, with the RBI Governor as Chairman, was set up in 1970 to formulate and review rural credit policies.
III. The Credit Guarantee Corporation of India was set up before the 1969 nationalisation to guarantee bank loans to small borrowers.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's profile of Governor L. K. Jha says the 1969 nationalisation was 'a step which did not have the endorsement of the Reserve Bank' (I). The Agricultural Credit Board, chaired by the Governor, was set up in February 1970 (II). The Credit Guarantee Corporation of India was established on 14 January 1971, after nationalisation, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – CGCI set up 14 Jan 1971
solution.why_others_wrong: Any option containing III is wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: 14 major commercial banks were nationalised in 1969, a step which did not have the endorsement of the Reserve Bank

Feb 1970: The Agricultural Credit Board set up with Governor as Chairman to formulate and review policies in the sphere of rural credit; 14 Jan 1971: Credit Guarantee Corporation of India Ltd. established

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Who was the twenty-first Governor of the Reserve Bank of India, serving from September 2003 to September 2008?

solution.explanation: RBI's list of Governors shows Dr. Yaga Venugopal Reddy, described as 'the twenty-first Governor', in office from 6 September 2003 to 5 September 2008. He was preceded by Dr. Bimal Jalan and succeeded by Dr. D. Subbarao (the 22nd).
solution.why_others_wrong: Dr. Jalan served 1997–2003, Dr. Subbarao 2008–2013 (22nd) and Dr. Rangarajan 1992–1997.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Dr. Y. V. Reddy

fact_checks.claim: Dr. Y V Reddy, 06-09-2003 to 05-09-2008: Dr. Yaga Venugopal Reddy the twenty-first Governor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which RBI Governor had served as India's Ambassador to the United States before joining the Bank?

solution.explanation: RBI's profile says Sir Benegal Rama Rau (Governor 1949–1957) 'served as the Indian Ambassador to the United States' before joining the Bank. L. K. Jha went the other way: he left the Governorship in 1970 on being appointed Ambassador to the US.
steps: Ambassador to US before RBI → Rama Rau
Ambassador to US after RBI → L. K. Jha
solution.why_others_wrong: L. K. Jha became Ambassador after his tenure; Deshmukh and Iengar were ICS officers who did not hold that post before joining.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Sir Benegal Rama Rau

fact_checks.claim: Sir Benegal Rama Rau ... Prior to joining the Bank he served as the Indian Ambassador to the United States
L K Jha was appointed India's Ambassador to the United States in May 1970 prior to the completion of his term as Governor

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI appointed Smt. Usha Janakiraman as Executive Director with effect from 1 December 2025. Which department was she assigned to look after?

options.text: Department of Supervision (Risk, Analytics and Vulnerability Assessment)
Department of Payment and Settlement Systems

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's College of Agricultural Banking at Pune was set up in September 1969 under a different name. What was it originally called?

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records the Cooperative Bankers Training College (CBTC), established at Poona (Pune) on 29 September 1969 to train the cooperative sector, which was renamed the College of Agricultural Banking in 1974.
steps: CBTC, Pune (1969) → renamed College of Agricultural Banking (1974)
solution.why_others_wrong: The Bankers' Training College (1954) was at Bombay; the Staff Training College (1963) at Madras; NIBM (1969) is a separate institute set up at Bombay.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Cooperative Bankers Training College

fact_checks.claim: 29 Sep 1969: Cooperative Bankers Training College (CBTC) established at Poona (Pune) to provide training to the cooperative sector. Later renamed College of Agricultural Banking (CAB) in 1974

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements based on RBI's profiles of its Governors:
I. Dr. D. Subbarao took over on 5 September 2008 as the 22nd Governor and was appointed for a three-year term.
II. Dr. Raghuram Rajan was Chief Economist and Director of Research at the International Monetary Fund between 2003 and 2006.
III. Dr. D. Subbarao had been a lead economist at the International Monetary Fund before becoming Finance Secretary.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's profile says Dr. Subbarao took over on 5 September 2008 as the 22nd Governor for a three-year term (I), and that Dr. Rajan was the IMF's Chief Economist and Director of Research in 2003–2006 (II). Dr. Subbarao was a lead economist at the World Bank (1999–2004), not the IMF, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – World Bank, not IMF
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option D: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: Dr. D. Subbarao took over on September 5, 2008 as the 22nd Governor of the Reserve Bank of India. Dr. Subbarao has been appointed for a three-year term ... lead economist in the World Bank (1999-2004)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about Shri Sanjay Malhotra, as given in RBI's profile:
I. Immediately before his appointment as Governor he was Secretary, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance.
II. He had earlier served on RBI's Central Board as a Government nominee director in 2022.
III. He is an Indian Police Service officer of the 1990 batch.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI's profile says that immediately before his appointment he was Secretary, Department of Revenue (earlier Secretary, Department of Financial Services) (I), and that he served on the Central Board as a Government nominee director from 16 February 2022 to 14 November 2022 (II). He is an IAS officer of the 1990 batch, Rajasthan cadre, so III is wrong.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Arrange the following institutions in the order in which they were set up, according to RBI's chronology:
I. Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR)
II. Bankers' Training College, Bombay
III. National Institute of Bank Management (NIBM), Bombay
IV. Staff Training College, Madras

solution.explanation: Bankers' Training College, Bombay: inaugurated 14 September 1954. Staff Training College, Madras: 26 August 1963. NIBM: established at Bombay on 24 September 1969 (later moved to Pune). IGIDR: established by RBI on 28 December 1987. Order: II, IV, III, I.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other orders misplace the 1963 Staff Training College or put IGIDR (1987) before NIBM (1969).
solution.final_answer: Option B: II, IV, III, I

fact_checks.claim: 14 Sep 1954: Bankers' Training College to provide training to banking personnel established at Bombay (Mumbai) inaugurated
26 Aug 1963: Staff Training College established at Madras
24 Sep 1969: National Institute of Bank Management (NIBM) established at Bombay (Mumbai)
28 Dec 1987: Indira Gandhi Institute of Development Research (IGIDR) was established by Reserve Bank

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's list of Governors gives these terms: Dr. D. Subbarao 05-09-2008 to 04-09-2013; Dr. Raghuram Rajan 04-09-2013 to 04-09-2016; Dr. Urjit R. Patel 04-09-2016 to 11-12-2018. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Dr. Rajan's tenure was the shortest, exactly 3 years
Dr. Patel's tenure was about 3 years and 3 months, the longest after Dr. Subbarao's
Dr. Patel's tenure was the shortest, about 2 years and 3 months, roughly 9 months less than Dr. Rajan's
All three served exactly one five-year term each

solution.explanation: Subbarao: Sep 2008 → Sep 2013 ≈ 5 years (1,825 days). Rajan: Sep 2013 → Sep 2016 = 3 years (1,096 days). Patel: 4 Sep 2016 → 11 Dec 2018 ≈ 2 years 3 months (828 days), about 268 days (≈9 months) less than Rajan's. Patel's was the shortest.
solution.why_others_wrong: Rajan's 3 years exceeds Patel's; Patel's tenure was not 3 years 3 months; the three terms differ.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Dr. Patel's tenure was the shortest, about 2 years and 3 months, roughly 9 months less than Dr. Rajan's

fact_checks.claim: Dr. D. Subbarao 05-09-2008 to 04-09-2013; Dr. Raghuram Rajan 04-09-2013 to 04-09-2016; Dr. Urjit R. Patel 04-09-2016 to 11-12-2018

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On the Mahatma Gandhi (New) Series banknotes, the raised (intaglio) identification mark for the visually challenged on the ₹500 note has which shape?

solution.explanation: RBI's currency FAQs list the identification marks in raised print: a horizontal rectangle for ₹2000, a circle for ₹500, a raised 'H' for ₹200 and a triangle for ₹100.
solution.why_others_wrong: The triangle is on ₹100, the horizontal rectangle on ₹2000 and 'H' on ₹200.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Circle

fact_checks.claim: There is an identification mark on the front side of each note which is in raised print (intaglio) and has different shapes for different denominations for e.g. Horizontal rectangle for ₹2000, circle for ₹500, raised Identification mark H for ₹200, triangle for ₹100

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Banknotes are printed at four presses. Where are the two presses owned by the Government of India through the Security Printing and Minting Corporation of India Ltd (SPMCIL)?

solution.explanation: Of the four currency presses, SPMCIL's are at Nashik (western India) and Dewas (central India); RBI's subsidiary BRBNMPL runs the presses at Mysuru and Salboni. Mumbai, Hyderabad, Kolkata and Noida host SPMCIL's coin mints.
solution.why_others_wrong: Mysuru and Salboni are BRBNMPL presses; the other cities are mints.
solution.final_answer: Option B: Nashik and Dewas

fact_checks.claim: The currency presses of SPMCIL are at Nasik (Western India) and Dewas (Central India). The two presses of BRBNMPL are at Mysuru (Southern India) and Salboni (Eastern India)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: What is a 'currency chest', as described in RBI's FAQs on currency management?

options.text: A storehouse at a select scheduled bank where banknotes and rupee coins are stocked on behalf of RBI for distribution to bank branches in its area
A vault at an RBI Issue Office where soiled notes are destroyed
A Government treasury where coins are minted
A locker in which customers keep foreign currency

solution.explanation: RBI authorises select scheduled banks to set up currency chests — storehouses where banknotes and rupee coins are stocked on RBI's behalf for distribution to bank branches in their area (2,691 as on 28 February 2025). Small Coin Depots stock coins below one rupee.
steps: Currency chest = bank-run store of RBI's notes and rupee coins for local distribution
solution.why_others_wrong: Note destruction happens at RBI; minting is done by SPMCIL; it is not a customer locker.
solution.final_answer: Option A: A storehouse at a select scheduled bank where banknotes and rupee coins are stocked on behalf of RBI for distribution to bank branches in its area

fact_checks.claim: the Reserve Bank has authorised select scheduled banks to establish currency chests. These are storehouses where banknotes and rupee coins are stocked on behalf of the Reserve Bank for distribution to bank branches in their area of operation. As on February 28, 2025, there were 2691 currency chests

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Which RBI offices, known as 'Mint Linked Offices', receive coins directly from the mints for onward distribution?

options.text: Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and New Delhi

solution.explanation: Coins minted by SPMCIL are received by RBI's offices at Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and New Delhi (Mint Linked Offices), which send them to other RBI offices and then to currency chests and small coin depots.
steps: Mints → Mint Linked Offices (Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai, New Delhi) → other offices → chests/depots
solution.why_others_wrong: Nashik and Dewas are note presses; Mysuru and Salboni are BRBNMPL note presses; the last set is not the list.
solution.final_answer: Option C: Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and New Delhi

fact_checks.claim: The Reserve Bank offices located at Hyderabad, Kolkata, Mumbai and New Delhi (Mint Linked Offices) receive coins from the mints

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In February 1964, a new Chapter IIIB was inserted in the RBI Act, 1934. What power did it give RBI?

options.text: To collect credit information from banks about their borrowers
To manage the foreign exchange reserves
To regulate the deposit acceptance activities of non-banking institutions

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records that on 1 February 1964 RBI was empowered to regulate the deposit acceptance activities of non-banking institutions through the new Chapter IIIB of the RBI Act — the base of its regulation of NBFCs.
steps: Chapter IIIB (1964) → deposit-taking by non-banking institutions
solution.why_others_wrong: Credit information powers came under Chapter IIIA (1962); co-operative banks came under RBI in 1966; forex management is unrelated to Chapter IIIB.
solution.final_answer: Option D: To regulate the deposit acceptance activities of non-banking institutions

fact_checks.claim: 1 Feb 1964: RBI empowered to regulate the deposit acceptance activities of non banking institutions. New chapter IIIB inserted in RBI Act
1962: Chapter IIIA incorporated in RBI Act empowered the Bank to collect information in regard to credit facilities granted by individual banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 12 January 1946, high denomination banknotes were demonetised to curb unaccounted money. Which denominations?

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology and currency FAQs record that ₹500, ₹1000 and ₹10,000 notes were demonetised in January 1946. Notes of ₹1000, ₹5000 and ₹10,000 were reintroduced in 1954 and demonetised again in January 1978.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1000/₹5000/₹10,000 is the 1978 set; ₹5000 notes did not exist in 1946; ₹100 notes were not demonetised.

fact_checks.claim: 12 Jan 1946: High Denomination Bank Notes of Rs 500, Rs 1000 and Rs 10,000 Demonetised to curb unaccounted money
₹500, ₹1000 and ₹10000 banknotes, which were then in circulation were demonetized in January 1946

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about pre-2005 series banknotes, according to RBI's currency FAQs:
I. Notes issued after the introduction of the MG series-2005 carry the year of printing on the reverse, which pre-2005 notes do not.
II. RBI's facility for exchanging pre-2005 notes is available only at specified offices of the Reserve Bank.
III. Banks cannot accept pre-2005 notes as deposits for credit to customers' accounts.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: MG series-2005 and later notes show the year of printing on the reverse (I). RBI's exchange facility for pre-2005 notes is available only at listed RBI offices (II). RBI clarifies that this does not mean banks cannot accept pre-2005 notes as deposits for crediting customers' accounts, so III is wrong.
steps: III: false – banks may accept them as deposits
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out the true statement II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

fact_checks.claim: banknotes issued after introduction of MG series-2005 have the year of printing on the reverse of the banknotes which is not present in the pre-2005 series

The exchange facility for pre-2005 banknotes is available only at the following offices of the Reserve Bank ... This, however, does not imply that banks cannot accept deposits of pre-2005 banknotes for crediting to the customers' accounts

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Commercial Banks – Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, on what basis must a bank calculate interest on domestic rupee savings deposits?

options.text: On the minimum balance between the 10th and the last day of the month
On the balance at the end of each quarter

solution.explanation: The Directions require interest on savings deposits to be calculated on a daily product basis, i.e. on the end-of-day balance. The older 'minimum balance between the 10th and last day' method survives only as a discretion for the composite cash credit account of a farmer.
steps: Savings deposit interest → daily product (end-of-day balance)
solution.why_others_wrong: The 10th-to-last-day minimum balance applies only to farmers' composite cash credit accounts; average monthly or quarter-end balances are not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option B: On a daily product basis

fact_checks.claim: Interest shall be calculated on a daily product basis
'Daily Product' means the interest applied on the end of day balance

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: From which date were banks advised to issue only CTS-2010 standard compliant cheques?

solution.explanation: RBI advised banks to issue only CTS-2010 compliant cheques from 30 September 2012. Separate clearing sessions for non-CTS cheques continued until 31 December 2018. CTS began in New Delhi on 1 February 2008, and the three grids merged into a National Grid on 13 October 2023.
solution.why_others_wrong: 1 Feb 2008 is the start of the New Delhi grid; 31 Dec 2018 the end of non-CTS clearing; 13 Oct 2023 the National Grid.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 30 September 2012

fact_checks.claim: Banks have been advised to issue only CTS-2010 standard compliant cheques from September 30, 2012

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: As defined in RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, a 'Notice Deposit' is a term deposit for a specific period that can be withdrawn on giving at least:

solution.explanation: A Notice Deposit is a term deposit for a specific period but withdrawable on giving at least one complete banking day's notice.
steps: Notice deposit → withdrawable after ≥ 1 complete banking day's notice
solution.why_others_wrong: Seven days is the minimum tenor of a domestic term deposit, not the notice period; the other periods are not in the definition.
solution.final_answer: Option D: One complete banking day's notice

fact_checks.claim: 'Notice Deposit' means term deposit for specific period but withdrawable on giving at least one complete banking day's notice

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's FAQs on cheque clearing, can a bank branch refuse to give an acknowledgement when a customer tenders a cheque for collection at its counter and asks for one?

options.text: No; banks must provide both a drop-box facility and an acknowledgement facility, and cannot refuse an acknowledgement at the counter
Yes; acknowledgements are given only for cheques above ₹1 lakh
Yes; if the bank has a cheque drop box, it need not give acknowledgements
No; but the bank may charge a fee for each acknowledgement

solution.explanation: Banks are required to provide both the cheque drop box facility and the acknowledgement facility at collection counters, and no branch can refuse an acknowledgement if the customer asks for it while tendering a cheque at the counter.
steps: Drop box AND acknowledgement facility both required
solution.why_others_wrong: There is no value threshold, the drop box does not replace the acknowledgement, and RBI does not mention a fee.
solution.final_answer: Option A: No; banks must provide both a drop-box facility and an acknowledgement facility, and cannot refuse an acknowledgement at the counter

fact_checks.claim: Banks are required to provide both the cheque drop box facility and the acknowledgement facility at their collection counters. No bank branch can refuse to give an acknowledgement to the customer if the latter asks for the same while tendering cheque for collection at the bank branch's counter

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank runs a term deposit scheme for resident Indian senior citizens offering higher, fixed rates. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, which of the following deposits is NOT eligible for it?

options.text: A term deposit of a resident Indian aged 62 held singly
A term deposit of a resident Indian aged 70 held jointly with his spouse
A term deposit in the name of an HUF whose Karta is a resident senior citizen
A term deposit of a retired staff member of the bank who is a resident senior citizen

solution.explanation: Banks may at their discretion run term deposit schemes for resident Indian senior citizens, but the facility is not offered on a term deposit in the name of an HUF or its Karta (as Karta), even if the Karta is a resident senior citizen. Retired staff who are senior citizens may even get the senior-citizen rate over and above their staff benefit.
steps: Senior citizen scheme → individuals, not HUF/Karta
solution.why_others_wrong: Individual resident senior citizens (single or joint) qualify, and retired staff senior citizens may get both benefits.
solution.final_answer: Option C: A term deposit in the name of an HUF whose Karta is a resident senior citizen

fact_checks.claim: A bank may, at its discretion, formulate term deposit schemes specifically for resident Indian senior citizens ... Provided that this facility is not offered on the term deposit standing in the name of an HUF or the Karta of the HUF, even if the Karta is a resident Indian senior citizen

A bank may, at its discretion, give its resident Indian retired staffs, who are senior citizens, the benefit of additional interest rates as admissible to senior citizens over and above the additional interest payable to them by virtue of their being retired members of the bank's staff

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Banks may offer term deposits without a premature withdrawal option. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, which deposits must nevertheless carry a premature withdrawal facility?

options.text: All term deposits of ₹3 crore and above (bulk deposits)
All term deposits from individuals (single or joint) of ₹1 crore and below
All term deposits of companies and trusts, whatever the amount
Only term deposits of senior citizens

solution.explanation: Banks are free to offer term deposits without a premature withdrawal option, but every term deposit accepted from individuals, held singly or jointly, for ₹1 crore and below must have the premature withdrawal facility.
steps: Exception: individuals' deposits ≤ ₹1 crore must be callable
solution.why_others_wrong: Bulk deposits (₹3 crore+) and deposits of companies can be non-callable; the protection is not limited to senior citizens.
solution.final_answer: Option B: All term deposits from individuals (single or joint) of ₹1 crore and below

fact_checks.claim: A bank shall have the freedom to offer term deposits without premature withdrawal option. Provided that all term deposits accepted by a bank from individuals (held singly or jointly) for amount of ₹1 crore and below shall have premature withdrawal facility

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Banks must enable the Positive Pay System for account holders issuing cheques of ₹50,000 and above. According to RBI's FAQs, for cheques of what value may banks consider making Positive Pay mandatory?

solution.explanation: Under Positive Pay, the drawer sends key cheque details to the bank in advance, and CTS cross-checks them. Availing it is at the account holder's discretion, but banks may consider making it mandatory for cheques of ₹5,00,000 and above.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹1 lakh is the free-collection limit for savings accounts; ₹2 lakh and ₹10 lakh are not RBI's thresholds here.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹5,00,000 and above

fact_checks.claim: Banks have been advised to enable PPS facility for all account holders issuing cheques for amount of ₹50,000 and above. While availing of this facility is at the discretion of the account holder, banks may consider making it mandatory in case of cheques for amounts of ₹5,00,000 and above

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 2 July 1966, soon after co-operative banks were brought under RBI's regulatory ambit, what change did RBI's chronology record for State Co-operative Banks?

options.text: 12 State Co-operative Banks were included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act
All State Co-operative Banks were converted into Regional Rural Banks
State Co-operative Banks were brought under DICGC deposit insurance
State Co-operative Banks were merged with NABARD

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records that co-operative banks came under RBI's regulatory ambit on 1 March 1966, and on 2 July 1966, 12 State Co-operative Banks were included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act.
steps: 1 Mar 1966 → co-op banks under RBI regulation
solution.why_others_wrong: RRBs came only in 1975; deposit insurance reached co-operative banks in 1971; NABARD was set up in 1982.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 12 State Co-operative Banks were included in the Second Schedule to the RBI Act

fact_checks.claim: 2 Jul 1966: 12 State Cooperative Banks included in Second Schedule of RBI Act
01 Jul 1971: Deposit Insurance cover extended to cooperative banks

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, by what time on each business day must a bank disclose on its website the interest rates it pays on bulk deposits?

options.text: 10:00 am, with a grace time up to 10:10 am
At the close of business of the previous day
12:00 noon, with a grace time up to 12:30 pm

solution.explanation: Deposit rates, including on bulk deposits, must follow the schedule disclosed in advance on the bank's website. Bulk deposit rates must be disclosed at 10:00 am, with a grace time of 10 minutes (latest 10:10 am), on each business day, and the bulk deposit rate card must be kept in the Core Banking System.
steps: Bulk deposit rate disclosure → 10:00 am (latest 10:10 am) daily
solution.why_others_wrong: The other timings are not in the Directions.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 10:00 am, with a grace time up to 10:10 am

fact_checks.claim: interest rates payable on bulk deposits shall be disclosed on the bank's website at 10:00 am with a grace time of 10 minutes, latest by 10:10 am, on each business day

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank sets fixed rates for FCNR(B) US dollar deposits for December 2026. The overnight Alternative Reference Rate for USD on the last working day of November is 4.30% (assume). Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what are the maximum rates it can offer on a 2-year and on a 4-year deposit?

solution.concept: Interest rate ceilings on FCNR(B) deposits
solution.explanation: Fixed-rate FCNR(B) deposits are capped with reference to the overnight ARR for the currency as on the last working day of the preceding month: ARR + 250 bps for 1 year to less than 3 years and ARR + 350 bps for 3 to 5 years. 4.30 + 2.50 = 6.80%; 4.30 + 3.50 = 7.80%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 6.80% for both ignores the higher ceiling for 3–5 years; 7.30%/8.30% and 5.30%/6.30% use wrong spreads.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 6.80% and 7.80%

fact_checks.claim: One year to less than three years: Overnight ARR for the respective currency / Swap plus 250 basis points; Three years and above upto and including five years: Overnight ARR for the respective currency / Swap plus 350 basis points

The Overnight ARR for the respective currency / SWAP rates as on the last working day of the preceding month shall form the base for fixing ceiling rates for the interest rates offered effective in the following month

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A depositor's unclaimed deposit of ₹7.5 lakh (with interest) had been moved to the DEA Fund when it was insured by DICGC (cover ₹5 lakh). The bank is now in liquidation and she claims the money. Under RBI's Miscellaneous Directions, how is the claim settled?

options.text: The Fund pays the entire ₹7.5 lakh to the liquidator in advance
DICGC pays her ₹5 lakh directly and the remaining ₹2.5 lakh is forfeited
The Fund pays ₹5 lakh to the liquidator, who pays her; the liquidator pays the remaining ₹2.5 lakh first and then seeks reimbursement from the Fund
She must claim from the bank's assets only, since the money is no longer in the bank

solution.concept: DEA Fund claims when a bank is in liquidation
solution.explanation: If the deposit was DICGC-insured when transferred, the liquidator claims from the Fund an amount equal to what could have been claimed from DICGC (₹5 lakh) and pays the depositor. The excess (₹2.5 lakh) is paid by the liquidator first and claimed from the Fund only by way of reimbursement.
steps: Insured part: min(7.5, 5) = ₹5 lakh paid by Fund upfront
Excess ₹2.5 lakh: liquidator pays, then is reimbursed
solution.why_others_wrong: The Fund does not prefund the excess; the amount is not forfeited; the claim is routed through the liquidator and the Fund, not the bank's assets alone.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The Fund pays ₹5 lakh to the liquidator, who pays her; the liquidator pays the remaining ₹2.5 lakh first and then seeks reimbursement from the Fund

fact_checks.claim: If the deposits of a customer / depositor were covered by DICGC insurance at the time of transfer to the DEA Fund, then the Liquidator can claim an amount equivalent to what could have been claimed from DICGC ... If the above deposit amount is more than the insurance cover of DICGC, then the Liquidator shall claim the amount in excess of DICGC insurance cover only on reimbursement basis

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Anu's term deposit of ₹2,00,000 at 7.00% matured, but she collected the proceeds only 73 days later. The bank's savings deposit rate is 2.50%. Under RBI's Interest Rate on Deposits Directions, 2025, what interest (simple, 365-day year) is due for the 73 days after maturity?

solution.concept: Interest on matured but unclaimed term deposits
solution.explanation: A matured, unpaid term deposit attracts the savings account rate or the contracted rate, whichever is lower. min(2.50%, 7.00%) = 2.50%: 2,00,000 × 2.5% × 73/365 = ₹1,000.
steps: Rate = lower of SB rate and contracted rate = 2.50%
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹2,800 uses the contracted 7%; interest is not nil; ₹1,900 uses neither rate.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹1,000

fact_checks.claim: If a Term Deposit (TD) matures and proceeds are unpaid, the amount left unclaimed with a bank, shall attract rate of interest as applicable to savings account or the contracted rate of interest on the matured TD, whichever is lower

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In a USD/INR buy/sell swap auction conducted by RBI (such as the USD 5 billion, three-year swap of May 2026), what does a participating bank do?

options.text: Buys US dollars from RBI now and sells them back later, absorbing rupee liquidity
Lends rupees to RBI against government securities
Borrows dollars from RBI to repay external loans
Sells US dollars to RBI now and agrees to buy the same amount back at the end of the swap, so rupee liquidity is injected for the tenor

solution.concept: FX swaps as a liquidity tool
solution.explanation: In a buy/sell swap from RBI's side, a bank sells US dollars to RBI and simultaneously agrees to buy the same amount back at the end of the swap period. RBI pays rupees in the near leg, injecting durable rupee liquidity for the swap's tenor; banks bid the premium they will pay to RBI.
steps: Near leg: bank sells USD, gets ₹ → liquidity injected
Far leg: bank buys back USD
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option describes a sell/buy (absorbing) swap; the others are not swaps.
solution.final_answer: Option D: Sells US dollars to RBI now and agrees to buy the same amount back at the end of the swap, so rupee liquidity is injected for the tenor

fact_checks.claim: The swap is in the nature of a simple buy/sell foreign exchange swap from the Reserve Bank side. A bank shall sell US dollars to the Reserve Bank and simultaneously agree to buy the same amount of US dollars at the end of the swap period

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under RBI's Commercial Banks – Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, which floating rate loans must be linked to an external benchmark, and what restriction applies to the choice of benchmark?

options.text: All floating rate personal or retail loans and floating rate loans to MSMEs; a bank must use one uniform external benchmark within a loan category
Only floating rate home loans; a bank may use different benchmarks for different borrowers in a category
All loans of all borrowers; the benchmark must be the bank's own MCLR
Only loans to micro enterprises; the benchmark must be the 91-day T-bill yield

solution.explanation: The Directions require all floating rate personal or retail loans (housing, auto, etc.) and floating rate loans to MSMEs to be benchmarked to an external benchmark. To ensure transparency and standardisation, a bank must adopt a uniform external benchmark within a loan category; multiple benchmarks within a category are not allowed.
steps: One external benchmark per loan category
solution.why_others_wrong: Coverage is wider than home loans and narrower than all loans; MCLR is internal; there is no single mandated benchmark such as the 91-day T-bill.
solution.final_answer: Option A: All floating rate personal or retail loans and floating rate loans to MSMEs; a bank must use one uniform external benchmark within a loan category

fact_checks.claim: All floating rate personal or retail loans (housing, auto, etc.), and floating rate loans extended by banks to Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) shall be benchmarked to an External Benchmark Rate
a bank must adopt a uniform external benchmark within a loan category; in other words, the adoption of multiple benchmarks by the same bank is not allowed within a loan category

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On 23 December 2025 RBI announced further measures to inject durable liquidity. What were they?

options.text: OMO purchases of ₹1,00,000 crore in two tranches and a USD 5 billion swap
A 100 bps cut in CRR and OMO sales of ₹50,000 crore
OMO purchases of ₹2,00,000 crore in four tranches and a three-year USD/INR buy/sell swap of USD 10 billion

solution.explanation: The 23 December 2025 announcement provided OMO purchase auctions of ₹2,00,000 crore in four tranches of ₹50,000 crore (29 December 2025 to 22 January 2026) and a USD 10 billion, 3-year buy/sell swap on 13 January 2026. The ₹1 lakh crore OMO and USD 5 billion swap were the earlier package of 5 December.
steps: 23 Dec 2025: OMO ₹2 lakh crore (4 × ₹50,000 crore) + USD 10 bn 3-yr swap
solution.why_others_wrong: The second option is the 5 December package; there was no CRR cut or OMO sale; the 90-day VRR came in January.
solution.final_answer: Option C: OMO purchases of ₹2,00,000 crore in four tranches and a three-year USD/INR buy/sell swap of USD 10 billion

USD/INR Buy/Sell Swap auction of USD 10 billion for a tenor of 3 years to be held on January 13, 2026

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Under the RBI MPC and Monetary Policy Process Regulations, 2016, at what time are the minutes of an MPC meeting released?

options.text: At 10 am on the 7th day after the meeting
At noon on the day of the policy announcement
At 5 pm on the last working day of the month
At 5 pm on the 14th day from the policy day (or the next working day if it is a holiday in Mumbai)

solution.explanation: Minutes, containing the resolution, each member's vote and their written statements (Section 45ZL), are released at 5 pm on the 14th day from the policy day, or the next earliest working day if that is a holiday in Mumbai.
steps: Minutes: 14th day, 5 pm (next working day if Mumbai holiday)
solution.why_others_wrong: The resolution (not the minutes) is released on the policy day; 7th day and month-end are not the rule.
solution.final_answer: Option D: At 5 pm on the 14th day from the policy day (or the next working day if it is a holiday in Mumbai)

fact_checks.claim: Minutes shall be released at 5 pm on the 14th day from the date of the policy day (or next earliest working day, if a holiday in Mumbai)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The MPC meeting originally scheduled for 5–7 August 2025 was rescheduled to 4–6 August 2025 'due to administrative exigencies'. Under which provision of the RBI Act was this announcement made?

solution.explanation: RBI announced the rescheduling under Section 45ZI(4) of the RBI Act, which deals with the meetings of the MPC (including publication of the meeting schedule). Section 45ZA concerns the inflation target, 45ZL the minutes and 45ZN the report on failure to meet the target.
solution.why_others_wrong: 45ZA (target), 45ZL (minutes) and 45ZN (failure report) do not deal with meeting dates.
solution.final_answer: Option A: Section 45ZI(4)

fact_checks.claim: Due to administrative exigencies, the MPC meeting has been rescheduled to August 4 – 6, 2025. This announcement is made under Section 45ZI(4) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: A bank's funds (other than equity) for computing MCLR are spread, from the longest maturity bucket down, as 15.1%, 11.8%, 9.3%, 16.9%, 24.3% and 10.5%. No single bucket exceeds 30%. Under RBI's Interest Rates on Advances Directions, 2025, to what tenor must its MCLR correspond?

options.text: The tenor of the largest bucket (24.3%)
The weighted average tenor of all six buckets
The weighted average tenor of the first three maturity buckets, which together first exceed 30% (36.2%)
The tenor of the first two buckets (26.9%)

solution.explanation: MCLR corresponds to the tenor of the single largest maturity bucket if it exceeds 30% of funds; otherwise to the weighted average tenor of two or more buckets that together account for more than 30%, taken cumulatively in descending order of maturity. Cumulative: 15.1, 26.9, 36.2 → the first three buckets.
solution.why_others_wrong: 24.3% is below 30%; all six buckets are not needed; two buckets give only 26.9%.
solution.final_answer: Option C: The weighted average tenor of the first three maturity buckets, which together first exceed 30% (36.2%)

fact_checks.claim: the weighted average tenor of two or more maturity buckets that together account for more than 30 percent, if no single maturity bucket accounts for more than 30 percent of the funds. The maturity bucket shall be arrived at by calculating the cumulative weightage based on the descending order of the maturity time buckets
For above-mentioned maturity profile of borrowings, the MCLR shall correspond to the weighted average of tenor of the first three time buckets

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The Governor's statement of 7 October 2026 said the 3-month T-bill, certificate of deposit (CD) and commercial paper (CP) rates averaged 5.29%, 6.33% and 6.91% since the August 2026 policy, against 5.28%, 6.73% and 7.08% between the June and August policies. Which statement is correct?

options.text: All three rates fell by about 40 bps
CD rates fell about 40 bps and CP rates about 17 bps, while the T-bill rate was almost unchanged (+1 bp)
CP rates fell the most, by about 40 bps
The T-bill rate rose about 17 bps while CD rates were unchanged

solution.explanation: Changes: T-bill 5.29 − 5.28 = +1 bp; CD 6.33 − 6.73 = −40 bps; CP 6.91 − 7.08 = −17 bps. With large surplus liquidity after August, private money market rates (CDs, CPs) moderated significantly.
solution.why_others_wrong: Only the CD rate fell by 40 bps; CP fell 17 bps; the T-bill rate barely moved.
solution.final_answer: Option B: CD rates fell about 40 bps and CP rates about 17 bps, while the T-bill rate was almost unchanged (+1 bp)

fact_checks.claim: The rates on 3-month treasury bill, 3-month certificates of deposit and 3-month commercial paper averaged 5.29 per cent, 6.33 per cent and 6.91 per cent respectively since August policy compared to 5.28 per cent, 6.73 per cent and 7.08 per cent, respectively during June and August policy

Five voted for 50 bps; Prof. Ram Singh voted for 75 bps

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's 7-day VRRR of 17 August 2026 (notified ₹2,00,000 crore) drew offers of ₹98,945 crore, all accepted at 5.24%; its 10-day VRRR of 9 October 2026 (notified ₹1,50,000 crore) drew ₹18,170 crore, all accepted at 5.49%. Which statement is correct?

options.text: About 49% of the notified amount was absorbed in August against about 12% in October, and the higher October rate reflects the repo rate having risen to 5.50%
Both auctions were oversubscribed, so partial acceptance applied
The October rate was higher because the SDF had been cut
About 12% was absorbed in August against 49% in October

solution.explanation: August: 98,945 ÷ 2,00,000 ≈ 49.5%; October: 18,170 ÷ 1,50,000 ≈ 12.1%. Both were undersubscribed, so all offers were accepted. Cut-offs sit just below the repo rate: 5.24% when repo was 5.25% (August) and 5.49% after the repo was raised to 5.50% on 7 October.
solution.why_others_wrong: Neither auction was oversubscribed; the SDF was raised, not cut; the shares are reversed in the last option.

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to a footnote in RBI's table of CRR changes, what special relief was given to banks for the 'millennium change' (Y2K)?

options.text: Cash in hand could be counted for CRR from 1 December 1999 to 31 January 2000, but not simultaneously for SLR
CRR was reduced to zero for one fortnight
Banks could count their SLR securities towards CRR

solution.explanation: To help banks tide over the millennium change, cash in hand maintained for CRR was treated as eligible for CRR for two months (1 December 1999–31 January 2000); that cash could not simultaneously count as an SLR asset. Normally CRR is a balance with RBI.
steps: Y2K: cash in hand counted for 2 months, not double-counted for SLR
solution.why_others_wrong: CRR was not suspended or cut to zero, and SLR securities never count for CRR.

solution.explanation: RBI's table shows SLR at 29% from 4 August 1972 and 30% from 17 November 1972, then 32% (December 1973) and 33% (July 1974).
solution.final_answer: Option C: 1972 (17 November)

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: According to RBI's chronology, by mid-1985 the statutory pre-emption of banks' resources through SLR and CRR together had exceeded:

solution.explanation: RBI's chronology records that by mid-1985 the combined SLR and CRR pre-emption exceeded 45%; after the CRR was raised to 15% in July 1989, it went above 53%.
solution.why_others_wrong: 53% was the 1989 level; 25% and 60% are not in the chronology.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 45%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: In 1992 SLR was 38.5% of net DTL as on 3 April 1992, plus 30% on any increase in net DTL over that level. A bank's net DTL was ₹1,000 crore on 3 April 1992 and ₹1,200 crore later in the year. What SLR assets did it need?

solution.explanation: Base: 38.5% × 1,000 = ₹385 crore. Increment: 30% × (1,200 − 1,000) = ₹60 crore. Total ₹445 crore — less than 38.5% on the whole ₹1,200 crore (₹462 crore), easing the burden on new liabilities.
solution.why_others_wrong: ₹462 crore applies 38.5% to all liabilities; ₹360 crore applies 30% to all; ₹385 crore ignores the increase.
solution.final_answer: Option D: ₹445 crore

fact_checks.claim: 38.5 + # (29-02-1992); + : SLR on net DTL as on April 3, 1992. # : In addition there was 30% SLR on the increase in net DTL over April 3, 1992 level

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's first Bank Rate (5 July 1935) was 3.5%. According to RBI's table, to what was it cut on 28 November 1935, a level that lasted until November 1951?

solution.explanation: The Bank Rate was cut to 3% on 28 November 1935 and raised back to 3.5% only on 15 November 1951.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other levels do not appear for that period.
solution.final_answer: Option D: 3%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: Amid the inflation of the oil-shock years, RBI's table shows the Bank Rate raised from 7% (31 May 1973) to what level on 23 July 1974?

solution.explanation: The Bank Rate went from 7% (31 May 1973) to 9% (23 July 1974) and stayed there until it was raised to 10% in July 1981.
solution.why_others_wrong: 10% came in 1981 and 12% in 1991; 8% is not the 1974 level.
solution.final_answer: Option B: 9%

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: RBI's table shows the Bank Rate at 12% from 9 October 1991, then 11% (16 April 1997), 10% (26 June 1997) and 9% (22 October 1997). What was the total cut in 1997, and what happened next?

options.text: 300 bps; it was raised by 200 bps to 11% in January 1998
300 bps; it was cut further to 8% in January 1998
100 bps; it was raised to 12% in 1998

solution.explanation: 12% → 9% in 1997 = 300 bps of cuts. On 17 January 1998, amid the Asian crisis, it was raised to 11%.
solution.why_others_wrong: The January 1998 move was an increase; the 1997 cut was 300 bps.
solution.final_answer: Option A: 300 bps; it was raised by 200 bps to 11% in January 1998

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: On which date did the Central Government first notify the 4% CPI inflation target (with 2%–6% tolerance band)?

solution.explanation: On 5 August 2016 the Government notified 4% CPI inflation as the target for 5 August 2016 to 31 March 2021. The first MPC was constituted on 29 September 2016; the first review was on 31 March 2021.
solution.why_others_wrong: 29 Sep 2016 is the MPC's constitution; 31 Mar 2021 the first review.
solution.final_answer: Option C: 5 August 2016

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The June 2026 MPC resolution noted that petrol and diesel prices had been raised cumulatively since May by 7.4% and 8.4%. What direct impact on headline CPI inflation did it estimate?

steps: Fuel price hikes → ~36 bps direct impact

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements about reviews of India's inflation target:
I. In its first review, on 31 March 2021, the Government retained the target and tolerance band for 1 April 2021 to 31 March 2026.
II. The second review was made on 25 March 2026.
III. RBI's Discussion Paper on the Review of the Monetary Policy Framework invited comments until 18 September 2026.
Which of the above is/are correct?

solution.explanation: RBI records the first review on 31 March 2021 (I) and the second on 25 March 2026 (II). The Discussion Paper was placed on 21 August 2025 with comments invited by 18 September 2025, not 2026, so III is wrong.
solution.why_others_wrong: Options with III are wrong; 'I only' leaves out II.
solution.final_answer: Option B: I and II only

Comments are invited on the questions raised in the Discussion Paper, from stakeholders and members of the public by September 18, 2025

questions.subject: Banking and Financial Awareness
questions.question_text: The MPC's projection of average CPI inflation for 2025-26 was 3.7% in June 2025, 3.1% in August 2025, 2.6% in October 2025 and 2.1% in February 2026. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It was cut by 110 bps between June and October 2025, and by 160 bps in all by February 2026
It was cut by 60 bps between June and October and by 110 bps by February
It was raised in every review
It fell by 160 bps between June and October 2025

solution.explanation: 3.7 − 2.6 = 1.1 points (110 bps) by October 2025; 3.7 − 2.1 = 1.6 points (160 bps) by February 2026.
solution.why_others_wrong: The other options misread the revisions; projections fell, not rose.
solution.final_answer: Option A: It was cut by 110 bps between June and October 2025, and by 160 bps in all by February 2026

fact_checks.claim: The average headline inflation for 2025-26 is now revised lower from 3.7 per cent and 3.1 per cent projected in June and August policy, respectively, to 2.6 per cent
